title: Decomposition
scenario: Each table has acceptance cases and a security or RAI plan. Eight fixes are on offer, and the budget covers about half of their cost.
why: Work items put every fix side by side with its acceptance cases and the controls that apply to it. Sprint planning picks from this list.
objective: Turn the PRD and the security and RAI backlog handoffs into a GitHub work-item plan that maps every acceptance case to one of FX-1 to FX-8.

tools.name: Functional Planner
tools.for: Plans a work-item hierarchy from the PRD. It's read-only: it writes a handoff file and creates nothing in a tracker

steps: Open [Investment Board](/#/board) and read the fix catalogue: FX-1 to FX-8, what each costs and what it risks.
Pick Functional Planner and send the prompt below.
Check that every acceptance case in your PRD lands on a work item, and that every work item names one fix.
Check that each control from your security or RAI backlog handoff sits on the work item it constrains.
Mark FX-7 and FX-8 as policy and process items with an owner outside the code. Keep the plan as a file: nothing is created in GitHub today.

prompts.label: Plan the work items
prompts.text: Plan a GitHub issue hierarchy for zava-silent-night from `docs/project-planning/zava-silent-night-prd.md`. Also read the backlog handoffs in `.copilot-tracking/security-plans/zava-silent-night/` and `.copilot-tracking/rai-plans/zava-silent-night/`. Map each work item to one fix from `data/fixes.json` (FX-1 to FX-8) and carry its acceptance cases. FX-7 and FX-8 are policy and process work. Write the handoff under `.copilot-tracking/github-issues/prds/` and don't create anything in GitHub.

ask: Which work item has no acceptance case yet?
Which security or RAI control would stop this fix from shipping?
Who owns FX-8 after the workshop ends?
mistakes: Splitting one fix into work items so small nobody can test them
Dropping the security and RAI items because they aren't code
step_in: When a table's plan has several work items per acceptance case

before: Check every table has a PRD and at least one backlog handoff. A table without one borrows a neighbour's.
Open the Investment Board on the trainer's screen with the budget at €150,000.

run.do: Show the fix catalogue: the eight fixes cost €295,000 together against a €150,000 budget.
Tables run Functional Planner. At 13:45, check FX-7 and FX-8 are in every plan.
Each table names one work item and its acceptance cases.

facilitator.good_answer: One work item per fix, each carrying its acceptance cases: for FX-1, the reference run's AC-001 to AC-003. Security control 8 (keep the exemption anchored to `defrost_until`) and RAI item WI-RAI-001 (remove the assistant's defrost-mode reassurance) sit on the fixes they constrain. FX-7 and FX-8 appear as policy items with owners in regional IT and store operations.
watch_for: Plans that leave out FX-6 because the assistant feels optional
Work items that copy the fix catalogue without the PRD's acceptance cases
facilitator.demo: Point at the five failure chips on the Investment Board and ask which failure has no fix on any table's plan.

done_when: Every acceptance case in your PRD appears on a work item
Every work item names one of FX-1 to FX-8
No issues were created in GitHub

stuck.if: Functional Planner asks which tracker to use
stuck.then: Answer GitHub, and tell it to plan only.

stuck.if: Your PRD covers only one failure
stuck.then: Plan work items for that failure and list the other fixes from `data/fixes.json` as placeholders.

handoff.note: Sprint planning reads the work-item plan, and each table picks one item for Day 3.
